extraction.rubric: docs/ruling-overreach-guard-design-2026-10-01/design.md §2.6 verbatim, with its §2.10 garble conventions, and design.md §2.6's reading for non-decision records: holding means 'states the record's own assertion within its scope'
conventions: holding: the record's own assertion, its point, stated within its scope. In a status record ('As of D, task X has status S') the status is that assertion, so it is a holding, not bookkeeping.
bookkeeping: an incidental who, when, which task, run, commit, escalation or file location that is not the record's assertion.
context: the grounds, measurements, mechanism, history or background a record gives for its assertion, including another task's plan described as background to a coordination rule.
A dropped 'As of D' on a status fact is not overreach (iv): graphiti carries the record's reference time as the edge's valid_at, and the status itself is unchanged.

overreach (iv) was applied when a dropped qualifier narrowed who, which or under what condition the assertion holds (e.g. 'a remediation pass's Stage 1', 'whichever lands second', 'In a .worktrees/<id> dispatch', 'Right').
A faithful fact on a generic or wrong endpoint ('task', 'Stage 2', a task the fact is not about) is misbound, per §2.10.

resolve_edge.rubric: design.md §2.6 resolve_edge gold: the duplicate set among the related facts, the contradicted candidates among related and invalidation candidates, or unjudgeable
conventions: duplicate: the related fact states the same proposition (same subject, relation and object) as the new fact, and the new fact adds no information the related fact lacks: phrasing-only differences, or the related fact is a strict refinement that entails the new one.
not a duplicate: the new fact adds a detail, an extra object, a different object/name, or a different relation.
contradicted: the candidate and the new fact cannot both hold of the same thing at the same time. A different plan, scope or time, or a merely related statement, is not a contradiction.
unjudgeable: the new fact or its candidates are too garbled to decide either question.

related facts are drawn from the new edge's own (source, target) node pair (luna_eval_frame.py::_resolve_fixture), so a related fact with a generic subject ('The code', 'The tests') is read as about the same two entities. (Added at fixture 031; fixture 004 re-checked under it before moving on.)
a later state that supersedes an earlier one on the same thing ('X survives only for Y' then 'X is deleted as Y no longer calls it') is a contradiction.

(refined at fixture 061, before 061 was written; 031 and 035 re-checked under it) an attribution wrapper describing the same end state ('The decision keeps/places X', 'e702d9e includes X') duplicates a new fact stating that end state. 'keeps X' differs from 'adds X' only when the new fact is about the change itself (035: 'The import additions ... include gc'). A future plan or proposal ('should', 'is proposed', 'will', 'can ... after') is not the fact that it is done.
(added at fixture 079) an evaluative add-on with no checkable content ('is now a stronger choice') is not added information; a factual qualifier (a condition, time, scope or object) is.

routing.rubric: design.md §2.6 routing: the correct label from the site's full vocabulary, which may be neither arm's
conventions: temporal_facts: the record's point is a status or a change event: "Task '...' completed. Landed in commit ...", "As of D ...", "no longer lives in X; moved to Y", "seeded ... on D".
entities_and_relations: the point is how code or project things are structured or connected, even when a task or plan is credited with it.
decisions_and_rationale: the point is a choice and why ("Decision: ...", ruled, chose, declined).
preferences_and_norms: a rule for how things should be done: a convention, a style or placement rule, a norm for addressing Leo.
procedural_knowledge: how to do something: steps, a workflow, a gotcha with how to avoid or reproduce it.
observations_and_summaries: a high-level takeaway or session recap, not one structural fact.
judged on the query's own wording against the prompt's cue phrases; a query that names a topic with no cue phrase is broad.

(added at item 042, before it was written; 031/033 already agree) a record that calls itself a gotcha is procedural_knowledge, the project's own category for gotcha-class entries, unless it is phrased as a convention or rule.
(added at item 085) a naming, style, shape or placement rule for tests is preferences_and_norms; "use helper X to do Y" is procedural_knowledge.
a "Completed: <title> / Description: ..." record is a completion event, like "Task '...' completed.": temporal_facts.
'conventions and gotchas for ...', or a query that asks for a convention, is preference ("what's the convention").
'blockers for: ...' is relational ("what depends on X").
'resolution for: ...' asks how an issue was settled; no type names that, so it is broad.
a task title, a review finding, a bug title or a keyword string over a topic is broad.
a short query (about 6 words or fewer) that names only specific identifiers (a symbol, file, field or device name) is entity_lookup ("what is X", "how are X and Y related").
'recent', 'history', 'since', 'what changed' make it temporal; 'status' alone does not.
an error message plus the command that hit it asks how to fix it: procedural.
